findings.description: The round-1 fix moved spend_recorder.record() into ReviewOrchestrator.dispatch_and_wait, which gets only an optional work_unit_ref and no change id. When the write fails, the spec spools to 'openspec/changes/<change-id>/reviews/spend-spool.jsonl' (spec line 173) and replay runs per change id. A dispatch_and_wait call with work_unit_ref None, such as a one-shot /parallel-review-* run or any caller not yet updated, has no change id, so the failed row has nowhere to go. That metered spend is then neither recorded nor spooled, which is the gap the fix was meant to close.
findings.resolution: Replace the bare work_unit_ref keyword with a spend context (change_id required, work_unit_ref optional) that converge() always passes, since it has change_id and the round, and that /parallel-review-* passes too. Without a spend context, dispatch_and_wait fails closed for metered lanes: no request is sent, and the result is vendor_unavailable with error 'spend_context_missing'. Add this to task 3.10 and the spec, with a scenario.

findings.description: The new 'spend context' row in the interface contract table says dispatch_and_wait adds 'work_unit_ref: str | None' and that a missing value only drops the field from the row. It does not carry the change id that the D4 spool path (openspec/changes/<id>/reviews/spend-spool.jsonl) needs, and it does not say what happens to a metered lane when no context is given.
findings.resolution: Change the row to 'spend_context: SpendContext | None = None' with change_id and an optional work_unit_ref. converge() always passes it (work_unit_ref from phase when known, otherwise from review_type). Without it, metered lanes are not dispatched (spend_context_missing), and non-metered lanes are unchanged. Add one sentence to D4.
